name: Payout reconciliation for an online store
summary: Each month the bookkeeper gets every payout from the store's processors and marketplaces taken apart and tied to the bank: the orders, refunds, chargebacks and fees inside it, each fee checked against the agreed rate, every difference listed with its evidence. A person posts the entries and raises any dispute.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's own rules for prepared work: the store's own exports as the only source, named column headings with a stop when one does not match, every difference listed with its evidence and never netted away, and a person who approves, posts and raises.

sources.contribution: Setting each payout against the orders inside it and the deposit it became; a payout smaller than its sales because fees, refunds, chargebacks and reserves come out first; a chargeback carrying its own fee; processor fees checked against the agreed rate separately; unsettled recent sales not treated as faults; amounts left in their original currency; exceptions settled only by a person.
Pairing records on an exact amount inside a window of days, and a tolerance expressed in cents, not as a share of the amount.

Each deduction compared with the channel's own fee table, kept current; fees grouped by kind; advertising held apart from the cost of selling; fees given as a share of sales; gross sales and fees recorded rather than the sum paid out; an overcharged fee as something that can be claimed back.
Gross sales, not the net payout, as the revenue figure; a fee rate given as a percentage and guarded so that it is not worked out when there are no sales.
